nodes.name: F-CDs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: CH4N2O (0.3g) and NH4F (0.092g) were dissolved in deionized water (30 mL). Then the solution was transferred to a Teflon autoclave (50 mL) and heated at 120°C for 6h. After natural cooling, the F-CDs were obtained.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of CDs: CH4N2O (0.3g) and NH4F (0.092g) were dissolved in deionized water (30 mL)... heated at 120°C for 6h.

nodes.name: F-CDs/CoCH/NF hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: 0.87g Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.3g urea, and 0.092g NH4F were completely dissolved in 30 mL deionized water solution under magnetic stirring. The Ni foam (2 cm × 3 cm) was cleaned with concentrated hydrochloric acid, ethanol, and deionized water before use. And then, the solution was transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave with a piece of Ni foam. Subsequently, the autoclave was sealed and maintained at 120°C for 6 h. After the autoclave was cooled at room temperature, F-CDs/CoCH/NF was collected and washed with water and ethanol several times and then dried at 60°C for 4 h.

nodes.name: F-CDs/CoP/NF phosphating
nodes.procedure: F-CDs/CoCH/NF was placed in the center of the high-temperature tube furnace, and approximately 1g of NaH2PO2 powder was placed in the upstream position. Then the tube furnace was heated from room temperature to 350°C at a rate of 3°C min^-1 in an Ar atmosphere, maintained at 350°C for 2 h, and then cooled to room temperature to obtain F-CDs/CoP/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show F-CDs/CoP/NF, Cl-CDs/CoP, and Br-CDs/CoP all match CoP (JCPDS 65-2593); precursors match CoCH (JCPDS 48-0083).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns in Figure 2a show that the composite's signals correspond well to reference values for CoP (JCPDS Card No. 65-2593)... All three showed XRD data (Figure S15b, Supporting Information) indexed to the characteristic peaks of CoP (JCPDS No. 65-2593).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows F-CDs/CoP/NF has urchin-like nanoneedle morphology covering NF, with unchanged nanostructure after phosphating; Cl-CDs/CoP shows Pinus bungeana-like structure; Br-CDs/CoP shows Albizia julibrissin-like structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The images indicate that the NF was totally covered by F-CDs/CoP nanoneedles... The SEM image of F-CDs/CoP (Figure 3a) shows a typical structure consistent with the reported needle-like morphology... Using Cl-CDs also gave assemblies of needle-like structures in a more divergent and robust nanocrystalline needle-like structure, similar to that of P bungeana... The morphology of Br-CDs/CoP appeared similar to a pair of symmetrical divergent A. julibrissin needles.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms needle-like assembly of F-CDs/CoP with cavities; F-CDs are ≈5 nm in diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image (Figure 2d) matches well with the SEM images, showing the needle-like assembly. Careful observation revealed different cavity sizes in the F-CDs/CoP needle-like structure... The TEM images in Figure S6, Supporting Information, in the Supporting Information show that the F-CDs were ≈5 nm in diameter.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of F-CDs/CoP shows 0.18 nm lattice spacing for CoP (211) plane and 0.21 nm for C (100) plane; similar single-crystal particles observed for Cl-CDs/CoP and Br-CDs/CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image of the electrocatalyst (Figure 2e) shows a uniform composite structure with F-CDs and CoP being well combined, the 0.18 lattice spacing corresponding to the (211) crystal plane of CoP... In addition, the image shows a lattice fringe of 0.21 nm, which is in good agreement with the (100) crystal plane of carbon.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Co, P, N, F, C in F-CDs/CoP nanorods; similar uniform distribution observed for Cl-CDs/CoP and Br-CDs/CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Element distribution mapping observed by high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM; Figure 2f-k) confirmed the presence of the elements Co, P, N, F, and C in the nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of F-CDs confirms elemental composition C, N, O, F; F-CDs/CoP shows Co, P, F, N, C, O with Co 2p (Co-O: 781.8/797.8 eV, Co-P: 778.5/793.5 eV), P 2p (129.6/130.4 eV, P-O: 134.1 eV), C 1s (284.8-289.0 eV), N 1s (400.2-402.5 eV), F 1s (687.0 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their elemental composition from XPS was C, N, O, and F (Figure S5, Supporting Information)... Figure S16, Supporting Information, shows that the F-CDs/CoP electrocatalyst is composed of Co, P, F, N, C, and O... The Co 2p fine structure spectrum of F-CDs/CoP is fitted by three typical components corresponding to Co-O (781.8 and 797.8 eV), Co-P (778.5 and 793.5 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle measurements show F-CDs/CoP/NF, Cl-CDs/CoP/NF, and Br-CDs/CoP/NF all exhibit superhydrophilicity with 0° contact angle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with NF (contact angle, 103°), F-CDs/CoP/NF exhibited surface hydrophilicity, as the contact angle reduced to 0°... Contact angle measurements for Cl-CDs/CoP/NF and Br-CDs/CoP/NF were also 0°.
